strict.criterion: Typical adult workers spend a majority of their time acquiring new knowledge/skills as a primary activity, not merely incidental learning while doing any job.
strict.rationale: BLS time-use evidence does not resemble a majority of time devoted to study/retraining. Continuing education remains important, but calling all productive work “learning” would make the forecast untestable. On an ordinary primary-activity reading it remains a miss.

evidence.title: BLS: Time use of millennials and nonmillennials
evidence.note: Time-use study separates work and educational activity. Does not fully count informal on-the-job learning, which is an interpretation limitation.

broader.criterion: Adult workers devote a substantial plurality or majority of their working hours to explicit education, training, and skill acquisition.
broader.rationale: Lifelong learning and occasional retraining matter in modern careers, but BLS time-use data show education and formal training represent only a tiny share of adult working time. Redefining routine job execution as 'learning' would make the claim impossible to falsify.
